config.grain_rationale: Each record is one QBCC licence held by a licensee (Licence Number + Licence Grade + Licence Class Type identify the licence; _id is the CKAN row id). The business participant is the licensee named in 'Licensee Name'. Licence-level attributes (grade, class, financial category) describe the licence, not the entity. The register is a flat export that never distinguishes a registered legal name from a trading name, so 'Licensee Name' is mapped only to entity.legal_name: for 'Company' rows it is the registered company name (corroborated by a checksum-valid ACN and PTY LTD suffixes), for 'Individual' rows it is the natural person who is the licensee. No trading name is claimed because the source provides none.

record_id.rationale: CKAN datastore row id; 508/508 distinct across the discovery partition and unique in held-out validation, so it identifies the licence record. Licence Number is not unique (506 distinct vs 508 rows), so it cannot be used alone.

fields.rationale: Single licensee-name column in a government licence register, mapped in full with no suffix heuristic and no suppression. Previous revision emitted only company-suffixed names here (7% coverage) and pushed personal names to trading_name; the reviewer rejected that split. An individual licensee is the natural person holding the licence, so its name belongs in legal_name rather than being dropped or relabelled as a trading name.

Direct source column in '99 999 999 999' shape; ABN checksum valid on 99.6% of discovery rows and 99.0% of held-out rows (1 and 6 rejections respectively). The abn transform strips separators and refuses to emit a checksum-invalid value, so bad source data surfaces as a counted error instead of a fabricated ABN. The residual ~1% rejections are reported honestly, not hidden.
All present values are '999 999 999'; 100% ACN checksum-valid in both discovery (34/34) and held-out (76/76) with zero errors. ACN is never derived from the ABN.

The source states the licensee type directly and 'C' -> company is well supported (ACN present, PTY LTD names). 'I' is deliberately NOT mapped to sole_trader after the reviewer rejected that inference (an individual licensee may be a partner or trust principal); 'I' rows therefore resolve to the ontology default 'unknown' rather than a guess.
Free-text single-line business address ending in state + postcode, e.g. '15 radiata pl Peregian Springs QLD 4573'. Passed through as stated by the source with whitespace normalisation only.

All addresses follow '<street> <suburb> <STATE> <postcode>'; the state token immediately before the trailing postcode is extracted and normalised by the state op (unknown -> OTHER). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 1080/1092 held-out rows emitted with zero errors.
Trailing numeric token of the address, validated by the postcode op (AU 4-digit, NT re-pad). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 100% coverage with zero errors in both partitions.

Reviewer P1 #1: 'Licence Type CODE' states whether the licensee is an individual (I, 474/508) or a company (C, 34/508). Recorded as matching evidence in holder_kind; it never implies sole_trader (entity_type keeps 'unknown' for I).
Publisher-assigned licence number, 100% present, identifies the licence across snapshots (506 distinct for 508 rows).

QBCC licence grade, six source-stated licence kinds: Trade Contractor Licence (462), Site Supervisor (23), Fire Occupational (9), Nominee Supervisor (7), Building Designer Licence (4), Mechanical Services Occupational (3).

Reviewer P1 #2: Licence Class Type is the licensed trade in the publisher's own wording (Carpentry, Plumbing and Drainage, Joinery, ...; 57 distinct, 100% present). Values are split on ', ' because the register packs multi-trade classes into one cell and ext.licence.class is multi-valued: one observed class per observation. Note this delimiter is also part of some single QBCC class names (e.g. 'Glass, Glazing and Aluminium'), so the split can fragment a compound publisher class - the dry run shows 531 observations from 508 rows (1.045 ratio) with zero errors; flag for the reviewer.

Licensed trade class is a source-stated activity mapped to ANZSIC 2006 only through the qbcc licence-class crosswalk, whose keys are the whole raw Licence Class Type strings (508/508 match, 0 errors). The unsplit value is used here so the crosswalk lookup matches; the same column also feeds ext.licence.class. scheme = anzsic2006.

SCT1 is the QBCC financial-category code 'Self Certification - Trade' and is a key of the qbcc_mfr band table (which now lists all 14 codes; this 508-row partition holds only SCT1). Value is the table label, scheme = qbcc_mfr. No period is stated by the source, so no period qualifier is emitted.

constants.rationale: Queensland Building and Construction Commission register; every address carries a QLD state code and an AU 4-digit postcode. Inferred from the publisher and address format rather than a source column, so confidence is moderate and flagged for review.

unmapped.reason: CKAN datastore row id for the licence record, not a business identifier; used only as record_id.
Human-readable duplicate of Licence Type CODE, which already feeds entity.entity_type (approved rule 3) and ext.entity.holder_kind; deduplicated.
Human-readable duplicate of Financial Category CODE, which feeds ext.financial.revenue_band; deduplicated.

config.notes:
REVISION after review. Advertised as CSV but the resource is a CKAN datastore_search API JSON envelope (starts '{"help":'), so format=json with record_path 'result.records'. No date column exists in the records: observation.observed_at falls back to resource last-modified metadata and no valid_from/valid_to can be supplied. Fixes for the reviewer's verdicts: (1) entity.trading_name REMOVED ('wrong' verdict - a personal licensee name is not a trading name, and for companies it duplicated the legal name); (2) the suffix-based legal_name heuristic REMOVED - 'Licensee Name' is now mapped in full to entity.legal_name (coverage 100%, no suppression, no guessing), which also resolves the 'doubtful' over-suppression of individual licensees; (3) entity.entity_type now maps only 'C'->company and lets 'I' fall to the ontology default 'unknown', removing the rejected 'I'->sole_trader inference; (4) address.locality REMOVED as brittle ('doubtful'), so address output is full/state/postcode only, all of which the reviewer rated 'ok'. Retained deliberately: entity.abn and entity.acn (direct, checksum-validated source columns rated 'ok'; ABN keeps a reported ~1% checksum rejection rather than hiding it) and address.country 'AU' at reduced confidence 0.8 and flagged. Open coverage gaps for a human: entity.trading_name (no trading name exists in this source), entity.status (no status column - register membership implies current licensing but that is inferred), entity.industry_code (no ANZSIC; Licence Class Type is the nearest but non-conforming signal), address.locality (unparseable from the free-text address), and no date fields at all.

[ext-v1] Revision of the rejected draft, addressing both P1 items and nothing else. (1) ext.entity.holder_kind from Licence Type CODE: I -> individual (474/508), C -> organisation (34/508), default unknown. Pure matching evidence; does not imply sole_trader, and the approved entity_type rule still maps I to 'unknown'. (2) ext.licence.class on the new licence role with the publisher's License Class Type wording, alongside the existing ANZSIC crosswalk rule (scheme = anzsic2006, table anzsic_qbcc_licence_class, 508/508 keys matched) on the business. (3) The full 195k-row register carries 14 Financial Category codes (qbcc_mfr now lists all of them); this 508-row snapshot holds only SCT1, so the rule is written generically to resolve other partitions through the same table. Everything else from the previous draft is kept: licence entity/role keyed on Licence Number, HOLDS_LICENCE relationship, ext.licence.number and ext.licence.grade. Approved rules 0-6 are untouched and not resubmitted. Personal names of individual licensees remain only in entity.legal_name (the licensee is the natural person holding the licence); no phone, email or trading name is claimed because the source provides none. Open item for the human reviewer: ext.licence.class uses split on ', ' to satisfy the multi-value gate, which fragments compound QBCC class names such as 'Glass, Glazing and Aluminium' (531 observations for 508 rows); the ANZSIC rule reads the unsplit value and stays 100% matched.

licence.rationale: Record grain is licence_or_permit; Licence Number identifies the licence across snapshots (506 distinct for 508 rows).

relationships.rationale: The licensee named in 'Licensee Name' holds the licence described by Licence Number / Grade / Class.

fields.reason: Licence Type CODE is genuinely a holder-kind marker (I/C). Mapping to individual/organisation with unknown default is correct and the rationale correctly says it does not imply sole_trader. A small risk that 'I' in QBCC means 'Individual' licensee while a company can hold through a nominee is not supported by evidence here, so the literal reading is acceptable.

Licence Number is a publisher-assigned licence identifier attached to the licence role; trimmed and null-if-empty is fine. 506 distinct for 508 rows means duplicate licence numbers exist; the licence key is therefore not unique, but the value itself is still a licence number, so only a note.

Licence Grade values (Trade Contractor Licence, Site Supervisor, Fire Occupational, Nominee Supervisor, Building Designer Licence, Mechanical Services Occupational) are indeed the publisher's licence kind and match ext.licence.grade; emitted on the licence role.

Splitting on ', ' fragments compound publisher classes rather than separating multi-valued classes. The mapping's own rationale admits the delimiter is part of single class names ('Glass, Glazing and Aluminium'), and the held-out record 70329 proves the damage: 'Fire Detection, Alarm and Warning Systems - Occupational' is emitted as two observations, 'Fire Detection' and 'Alarm and Warning Systems - Occupational', neither of which is a licensed class. The correct single value is the whole cell. Rule 4 correctly reads the unsplit cell; rule 3 must not split. Use the cell as one observation, or split only on a delimiter proven to separate classes (there is none documented).

Direction is right (unsplit raw class -> ANZSIC 2006 via a reviewed crosswalk with scheme qualifier anzsic2006), and keeping the cell unsplit is correct here. But the crosswalk is flagged 'draft - judgement crosswalk prepared by an AI assistant', derivation L2 with 31 literal keys plus regex patterns for the rest, and the emitted codes are heterogeneous in precision: '30' (2-digit subdivision) for Builder - Low Rise, '3231'/'3243'/'3291' as 4-digit groups, and '6921' for Building Design - Medium Rise. ANZSIC 6921 is 'Architectural Services' (few-digit precision mixing is allowed by the pattern, but '30' alone for a low-rise builder and 3243 for both Floor Finishing and Wall and Floor Tiling need human confirmation). Also, a trade class is the licensed trade performed, not the entity's own industry for supervisory/nominee grades; the industry_code attaches to business, so association is arguable. Acceptable only after human review of the crosswalk.

QBCC 'Financial Category' (SCT1 = Self Certification - Trade) is the licensee's financial requirement category / maximum contract value threshold band, not revenue or turnover of the business. ext.financial.revenue_band is defined as a revenue/turnover band of a named scheme; 'Self Certification - Trade' is a self-certification category whose max contract value is not a turnover band. Additionally the emitted label is prefixed 'SCT1: ' while the ontology says the value must be a label of the scheme's own crosswalk table, and the crosswalk is marked 'turnover caps NOT verified' with scheme null. Mapping the financial category code to a revenue band overstates what the source states.

missed.reason: Its being treated as a pure duplicate of Licence Type CODE should be verified; if any DESC value contradicts CODE (e.g. states 'Individual' vs a company style), holder_kind would be wrong for those rows. Cheap corroboration column.

The human-readable financial category description is the publisher's own wording for the band and should be kept as evidence or raw_value rather than dropped, given the band label emitted is a synthesized 'SCT1: ...' string.

critic.summary: Rules 0-2 are sound: holder_kind, licence.number and licence.grade attach to the correct role and mean what the ontology means. Rule 3 is wrong: splitting Licence Class Type on ', ' fragments compound QBCC class names, producing fabricated classes in the held-out data (record 70329 becomes 'Fire Detection' + 'Alarm and Warning Systems - Occupational' instead of one class). Rule 4 is directionally correct and correctly uses the unsplit cell, but is doubtful because its ANZSIC crosswalk is a draft AI judgement table mixing 2- and 4-digit precision codes and treating a licensed trade as the business's industry for supervisor/nominee grades; needs human sign-off. Rule 5 is wrong: the QBCC financial category (SCT1 'Self Certification - Trade') is a financial requirement/contract-value category, not a revenue or turnover band, and the emitted label is a synthesized 'SCT1: ...' string that is not a plain key label of the qbcc_mfr table; the scheme also claims turnover caps not verified. The overlapping use of the same column by rules 3 and 4 is fine in principle. No personal contact data appears in the emitted claims.

new_rules.rationale: Single licensee-name column in a government licence register, mapped in full with no suffix heuristic and no suppression. Previous revision emitted only company-suffixed names here (7% coverage) and pushed personal names to trading_name; the reviewer rejected that split. An individual licensee is the natural person holding the licence, so its name belongs in legal_name rather than being dropped or relabelled as a trading name.

Direct source column in '99 999 999 999' shape; ABN checksum valid on 99.6% of discovery rows and 99.0% of held-out rows (1 and 6 rejections respectively). The abn transform strips separators and refuses to emit a checksum-invalid value, so bad source data surfaces as a counted error instead of a fabricated ABN. The residual ~1% rejections are reported honestly, not hidden.
All present values are '999 999 999'; 100% ACN checksum-valid in both discovery (34/34) and held-out (76/76) with zero errors. ACN is never derived from the ABN.

The source states the licensee type directly and 'C' -> company is well supported (ACN present, PTY LTD names). 'I' is deliberately NOT mapped to sole_trader after the reviewer rejected that inference (an individual licensee may be a partner or trust principal); 'I' rows therefore resolve to the ontology default 'unknown' rather than a guess.
Free-text single-line business address ending in state + postcode, e.g. '15 radiata pl Peregian Springs QLD 4573'. Passed through as stated by the source with whitespace normalisation only.

All addresses follow '<street> <suburb> <STATE> <postcode>'; the state token immediately before the trailing postcode is extracted and normalised by the state op (unknown -> OTHER). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 1080/1092 held-out rows emitted with zero errors.
Trailing numeric token of the address, validated by the postcode op (AU 4-digit, NT re-pad). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 100% coverage with zero errors in both partitions.
Publisher-assigned licence number, 100% present, identifies the licence across snapshots.
QBCC licence grade: Trade Contractor Licence, Site Supervisor, Fire Occupational, Nominee Supervisor, Building Designer Licence, Mechanical Services Occupational.
Licensed trade class is a source-stated activity mapped to ANZSIC 2006 only via the qbcc licence-class crosswalk, whose keys are the whole raw Licence Class Type strings (508/508 match, 0 errors).
SCT1 is the QBCC financial category code; qbcc_mfr band table has key SCT1.

unmapped.reason: CKAN datastore row id for the licence record, not a business identifier; used only as record_id.
